facts.summary: Virginia's minimum wage is $12.77 per hour effective January 1, 2026 (or the federal minimum if higher), rising to $13.75 in 2027 and $15.00 in 2028.
facts.sourceAgency: Virginia General Assembly (official Code of Virginia)
facts.notes: Higher than the federal $7.25. Figure is the statutory schedule amount for calendar year 2026; annual CPI-based adjustments begin in 2029.

facts.summary: Virginia has no daily overtime or higher salary floor; the Virginia Overtime Wage Act incorporates the federal FLSA overtime requirements, exemptions, and calculation methods by reference.
facts.sourceAgency: Virginia General Assembly (official Code of Virginia)
facts.notes: As amended, Virginia overtime tracks FLSA (OT after 40 hrs/week). State-law overtime actions have a 3-year statute of limitations.

value: pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions including lactation
facts.summary: The Virginia Human Rights Act protects several classes beyond the federal set, including sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, pregnancy/childbirth/lactation, military status, and ethnic origin.
facts.sourceAgency: Virginia General Assembly (official Code of Virginia)
facts.notes: Full statutory list also includes race, color, religion, sex, age, disability, and national origin (federally covered). 'Age' is defined as 40 or older.

facts.summary: The Virginia Human Rights Act's core employment discrimination provisions cover employers with five or more employees (and employers of one or more domestic workers), lower than the federal 15-employee threshold under Title VII.
facts.sourceAgency: Virginia General Assembly (official Code of Virginia)
facts.notes: Threshold is 5+ employees for each working day in each of 20+ calendar weeks in the current or preceding year; 1+ for domestic-worker employers. Some specific claims may have differing thresholds.

facts.value: required for employers with more than five employees
facts.summary: Virginia law requires employers to provide reasonable accommodation for a qualified person's known disability and to engage in a timely, good-faith interactive process when accommodation is requested.
facts.sourceAgency: Virginia General Assembly (official Code of Virginia)
facts.notes: Applies to employers with more than five employees. The explicit statutory interactive-process mandate is an addition beyond the federal ADA framework.

facts.value: Va. Code § 40.1-27.3 protects employees from retaliation
facts.summary: Virginia's whistleblower statute bars employers from discharging, disciplining, or otherwise retaliating against employees who report legal violations, participate in investigations, refuse illegal acts, or testify to government bodies.
facts.sourceAgency: Virginia General Assembly (official Code of Virginia)
facts.notes: Employees must sue within one year; remedies include reinstatement, back pay with interest, attorney fees, and injunctive relief.

facts.summary: A civil action for unpaid wages under Virginia's wage payment law must be commenced within three years after the cause of action accrued.
facts.sourceAgency: Virginia General Assembly (official Code of Virginia)
facts.notes: The limitations period is tolled while an administrative complaint is pending. The overtime action limitations period (§ 40.1-29.2) is also three years.

facts.summary: An employment discrimination complaint under the Virginia Human Rights Act must be filed with the Office of Civil Rights no later than two years after the alleged discriminatory practice occurred.
facts.sourceAgency: Office of Civil Rights, Virginia Office of the Attorney General (Department of Law)
facts.notes: Longer than the federal EEOC 180/300-day deadlines. Verify any separate shorter deadline that may apply to dual-filed EEOC charges.

facts.summary: On termination, Virginia employers must pay all wages due for prior work on or before the date the employee would have been paid had employment continued (i.e., the next regular payday).
facts.sourceAgency: Virginia General Assembly (official Code of Virginia)
facts.notes: Applies to both voluntary and involuntary separation. No immediate same-day final-pay requirement.
